Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_psexec:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'
    selection_wmic_remote:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wmic.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '/node:'
    condition: selection_psexec or selection_wmic_remote
falsepositives:
    - Sysadmins running approved remote-management tooling — wrap with
      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] GitHub Actions runner outbound to gist.githubusercontent.com (tj-actions/changed-files CVE-2025-30066)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
GitHub Actions runner outbound to gist.githubusercontent.com (tj-actions/changed-files CVE-2025-30066) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts a self-hosted CI/CD runner process (Runner.Worker/node/python/curl) reaching gist.githubusercontent.com — the exact egress the compromised tj-actions/changed-files action used to pull its memory-dumping Python second stage. This was StepSecurity Harden-Runner's original detection signal for the March 2025 incident. Rationale: Uses the corroborated network IOC (outbound to gist.githubusercontent.com from a runner) that StepSecurity's Harden-Runner used to detect CVE-2025-30066; scoped to runner process ancestry (Runner.Worker/node/python/_actions paths) to separate it from ordinary developer gist fetches. Cross-checked against CISA, Wiz and Sysdig write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/03/18/supply-chain-compromise-third-party-tj-actionschanged-files-cve-2025-30066-and-reviewdogaction • https://www.wiz.io/blog/github-action-tj-actions-changed-files-supply-chain-attack-cve-2025-30066 • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/detecting-and-mitigating-the-tj-actions-changed-files-supply-chain-attack-cve-2025-30066
ATT&CKT1105 T1195.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A build step legitimately curls a config/install script hosted on a GitHub gist
  • Developer tooling or dotfiles bootstrap that pulls from gist.githubusercontent.com on a self-hosted runner
  • Package post-install hooks fetching helper scripts from a gist
  • Security tooling / EDR test harness deliberately reaching gist domains
  • Renovate/Dependabot-style automation resolving raw gist content
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("renovate","dependabot") or RemoteUrl has "raw.githubusercontent.com/your-org")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full command line and parent chain of the initiating process; confirm it ran inside a GitHub Actions job (Runner.Worker/_work/_actions path) and identify the workflow/repo. Grab the exact gist URL and the resolved IP. 2) Contain: if the job used tj-actions/changed-files (or any action pinned to a mutable tag), pause the runner, and immediately rotate every secret exposed to workflows that ran between 2025-03-12 00:00 and 2025-03-15 12:00 UTC (access keys, GitHub PATs, npm tokens, RSA keys). 3) Hunt: search the same runner fleet for the malicious commit 0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67 and for double-base64 blobs written to workflow logs; review runner egress for other first-seen domains.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "gist.githubusercontent.com" or RemoteUrl has "gist.github.com"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","python.exe","python3","python","curl.exe","curl","wget","Runner.Worker.exe","Runner.Worker")
     or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("Runner.Worker.exe","Runner.Worker","node.exe","node")
     or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("actions-runner","_work","_actions")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "gist.githubusercontent.com" or HttpHostName in~ ("gist.githubusercontent.com","gist.github.com")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstIpAddr
| order by TimeGenerated desc

tj-actions/changed-files malicious commit 0e58ed86 referenced on host (CVE-2025-30066) AIDelivery High
Alerts on the exact malicious tj-actions/changed-files commit SHA (0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67) appearing in any process command line or file path on a self-hosted runner — i.e. the compromised action being fetched, checked out, or pinned. A pure, second-source-confirmed IOC hunt for the retagged supply-chain payload. Rationale: Uses the article's SHA1 (0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67), independently confirmed by CISA and the GitHub Advisory as the single malicious commit every tj-actions/changed-files tag (v1.0.0–v44.5.1) was pointed to — a unique, zero-ambiguity IOC that only appears when the compromised action is fetched, checked out, or SHA-pinned. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/ghsa-mrrh-fwg8-r2c3 • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2025/03/18/supply-chain-compromise-third-party-tj-actionschanged-files-cve-2025-30066-and-reviewdogaction • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/github-actions-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC/threat-intel tooling scanning for the hash as an IOC (grep, EDR IOC sweep) surfaces the string in its own command line
  • A remediation script that greps repos/workflows for the malicious SHA
  • Vulnerability-management agent enumerating the commit as data
  • A security researcher reproducing/analyzing the incident in a lab runner
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("grep.exe","findstr.exe","rg.exe","select-string") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("IOC","threat-intel","scan-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the SHA appears in a real action fetch/checkout (Runner.Worker/git/_actions context) versus an analyst's own IOC-scan process; identify the repo and the workflow run time. 2) Contain: treat the runner and any workflow that executed the action as compromised — rotate all secrets exposed to workflows run between 2025-03-12 00:00 and 2025-03-15 12:00 UTC, and repin tj-actions/changed-files to the patched v46.0.1 by full SHA. 3) Hunt: pivot to outbound gist.githubusercontent.com egress from the same runner, inspect workflow logs for double-base64 secret blobs, and check for the sibling reviewdog/action-setup CVE-2025-30154 across the fleet.
let ioc = "0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67";
union
 (DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has ioc or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has ioc
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ProcessEvent", Account=AccountName, Evidence=ProcessCommandLine, Context=InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
 (DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
  | where FolderPath has ioc or FileName has ioc or FolderPath has "tj-actions/changed-files"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="FileEvent", Account=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Evidence=FolderPath, Context=InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67") or SHA1 in~ ("0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67") or MD5 in~ ("0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67") or SHA1 in~ ("0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67") or MD5 in~ ("0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["0e58ed8671d6b60d0890c21b07f8835ace038e67"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TeamPCP Trivy/KICS supply-chain credential exfil to scan.aquasecurtiy.org & 45.148.10.212 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections from CI/CD runners (or any onboarded host) to the exact exfiltration infrastructure used by TeamPCP's compromised aquasecurity/trivy-action and Checkmarx KICS actions. Any egress to these hard IOCs means the credential stealer's POST reached the wire. Rationale: Anchored on the article's verbatim exfil host scan.aquasecurtiy.org (typosquat resolving to 45.148.10.212) plus the pre-extracted secondary IOC IPs/domains; connection to any is near-zero-FP and confirms secrets left the runner.
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A security researcher deliberately detonating the compromised action in a sandbox
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling actively resolving/probing the IOC domains
  • A blocked/failed connection logged by a proxy that never actually exfiltrated
  • Internal typosquat-monitoring service crawling lookalike domains
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host/runner and the InitiatingProcess making the connection; confirm whether it is a CI runner that recently executed aquasecurity/trivy-action or Checkmarx KICS. 2) Contain: isolate the runner, rotate ALL secrets/tokens exposed to that job (GITHUB_TOKEN, cloud OIDC creds, registry creds) and revoke active sessions. 3) Hunt: pull every repo/workflow that referenced the compromised action across the org, pivot on the /proc/pid/mem credential-harvest UC, and block the IOC IPs/domains at egress.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc

| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, DvcAction, NetworkBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Credential harvest via /proc/<pid>/mem read of GitHub Actions Runner.Worker AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the core TeamPCP payload behaviour: a spawned interpreter (python/node/sh) reading /proc/<pid>/mem of the Runner.Worker process to scrape marked secrets from runner memory. This is the article's exact credential-access primitive, independent of the exfil endpoint. Rationale: Uses the article's exact TTP — a payload process reading /proc/pid/mem of the Runner.Worker process — as the pivot; the Runner.Worker parent + interpreter + /proc/*/mem triad is specific to CI runner memory-scraping and rarely legitimate.
ATT&CKT1003.007 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate profiling/debugging tools (gdb, py-spy) attached to a runner job by a maintainer
  • Crash-dump or coredump collection tooling reading /proc during a CI failure
  • Custom self-hosted-runner health scripts inspecting worker memory usage
  • Security agents themselves reading /proc for telemetry
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("py-spy","gdb","coredumpctl","/usr/bin/perf"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full ProcessCommandLine and the target PID; confirm the parent is the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker and the child interpreter is not part of the declared workflow. 2) Contain: kill the job, isolate the runner, and immediately rotate every secret injected into that workflow run plus any downstream cloud OIDC tokens. 3) Hunt: correlate to the C2 egress UC (scan.aquasecurtiy.org/45.148.10.212) within the same job window, and enumerate all repos referencing aquasecurity/trivy-action or Checkmarx KICS by tag.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "Runner.Worker" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker" or ProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker"
| where FileName in~ ("python","python3","node","sh","bash","perl","ruby")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "mem"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has "Runner.Worker" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "Runner.Worker"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","node","sh","bash","perl","ruby")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "mem"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GitHub Actions Runner.Worker Memory Scrape via /proc/pid/mem
id: c1d4e7a2-5b62-4f18-8a90-77e3b1c2f6d0
description: Detects an interpreter spawned by the GitHub Actions Runner.Worker process reading /proc/<pid>/mem to extract secrets from runner memory, matching TeamPCP's trivy-action credential stealer.
references:

      - '/node'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'

DNS resolution of TeamPCP typosquat exfil domain scan.aquasecurtiy.org AICommand & Control High
Hunts DNS lookups for the misspelled typosquat scan.aquasecurtiy.org (impersonating aquasecurity) and the other TeamPCP staging/exfil domains. Catches the campaign at name-resolution even when egress is blocked or the C2 IP rotates. Rationale: The domain scan.aquasecurtiy.org is an intentional typosquat of aquasecurity called out verbatim in the article; resolving it (or the other named TeamPCP domains) is a high-fidelity, rotation-resistant signal that survives IP changes.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Typosquat-monitoring / brand-protection service resolving lookalike domains
  • Malware sandbox or IOC-validation pipeline resolving the domains
  • Passive-DNS collector or threat-intel feed enrichment
  • DNS sinkhole logging the query after redirect
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the querying host and the initiating process; determine if it is a CI runner mid-workflow vs a research/monitoring system. 2) Contain: sinkhole/block the domains org-wide, isolate the runner, and rotate secrets scoped to any workflow that ran on that host. 3) Hunt: pivot to the resolved IP against the C2-connection UC, and check whether the /proc/pid/mem harvest fired on the same host within the job window.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("scan.aquasecurtiy.org","checkmarx.zone","audit.checkmarx.cx","models.litellm.cloud","tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai.raw.icp0.io")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any ("scan.aquasecurtiy.org","checkmarx.zone","audit.checkmarx.cx","models.litellm.cloud","tdtqy-oyaaa-aaaae-af2dq-cai.raw.icp0.io")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName, DnsResponseCodeName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

GitHub Actions runner spawns network tool / interpreter under compromised trivy-action or KICS AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the execution stage of the supply-chain payload: the Runner.Worker (or a trivy/kics action step) spawning curl/wget/python/node that then reaches the internet — the shape a weaponized aquasecurity/trivy-action or Checkmarx KICS tag exhibits when it stages/exfils. Rationale: Grounds on the article's named compromised actions (aquasecurity/trivy-action, Checkmarx KICS) and the Runner.Worker process; a scanner action shelling out to curl/wget/python for outbound POSTs is off-pattern for legitimate SCA/SBOM tooling.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate trivy DB update fetching vulnerability feeds via curl/wget over HTTPS
  • A workflow step that legitimately uses python/node to post results to an internal dashboard
  • Self-hosted runner bootstrap scripts pulling dependencies
  • Container image scan steps that curl a registry manifest
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("aquasec.com","ghcr.io","github.com","trivy-db","vulnerability-db") and not ProcessCommandLine has "scan.aquasecurtiy")
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the ChildProcessCommandLine destination — is it an official aquasecurity/checkmarx endpoint or an unknown/typosquat host? Cross-check the action tag/ref used against the known-compromised list. 2) Contain: cancel the run, isolate the runner, rotate secrets exposed to the job, and pin/replace the action to a verified SHA. 3) Hunt: correlate to the C2, DNS, and /proc/pid/mem UCs on the same host+job, and org-wide enumerate every workflow referencing the compromised action by mutable tag.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "Runner.Worker" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("trivy","trivy-action","kics")
| where FileName in~ ("curl","wget","python","python3","node","nc","ncat")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","-d ","--data","POST","/proc/","scan.aquasecurtiy")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has "Runner.Worker" or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("trivy","trivy-action","kics")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","python","python3","node","nc","ncat")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","--data","POST","/proc/","scan.aquasecurtiy")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

easy-day-js second-stage C2 beacon to Mastra supply-chain infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts outbound connections to the hardcoded C2 IPs and domains used by the second-stage payload dropped by the malicious easy-day-js typosquat during the June 2026 Mastra npm compromise. Any host reaching 23.254.164.92/.123, teams.onweblive.org or maskasd.com is a confirmed post-install callback. Rationale: Uses the five article-supplied network IOCs (23.254.164.92, 23.254.164.123, teams.onweblive.org, maskasd.com) that are the dropper's second-stage callback destinations — exact-match on attacker infra is inherently high-fidelity.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher / sandbox detonating the sample from a corporate host
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling actively resolving the IOC domains
  • Recycled hosting IP later reassigned to a benign tenant on 23.254.164.0/24
  • Proxy/egress appliance logging the block as an allowed-then-denied event
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") // exclude analyst manual IOC lookups in a browser
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process — if node.exe/npm confirms a compromised dependency install; pull the host's package tree and the Secure Registry Policy Evaluations log for that device. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block 23.254.164.92/.123 and the two domains at egress, revoke any credentials/tokens present on the machine or CI runner. 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the same RemoteIP/RemoteUrl and for node_modules/easy-day-js, and for any host that pulled a Mastra-ecosystem package in the exposure window.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.254.164.92", "23.254.164.123") or RemoteUrl in~ ("teams.onweblive.org", "maskasd.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("23.254.164.92", "23.254.164.123") or DstHostname in~ ("teams.onweblive.org", "maskasd.com")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm/node postinstall script spawning a download or shell process (Mastra dropper pattern) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the obfuscated postinstall dropper behaviour from the easy-day-js compromise: the npm/node package-manager process spawning powershell/curl/certutil/cmd to pull a second-stage payload immediately after install. Targets the parent→child chain rooted in node_modules. Rationale: Grounds on the article's described TTP — an obfuscated postinstall dropper that fetches a second-stage from an attacker server — expressed as the node/npm parent spawning a download/shell child in node_modules context. Behavioural, not IOC-bound, so it catches future variants.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native-module packages (node-gyp) shelling out to cmd/python during install
  • Dev tooling that runs curl in a postinstall to fetch platform binaries (e.g. puppeteer, esbuild)
  • CI runners executing lifecycle scripts that legitimately call PowerShell
  • Corporate npm packages with signed postinstall bootstrap scripts
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild-install","puppeteer") and ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("iex","-enc","FromBase64String"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the child command line — a URL to a non-registry host or base64/obfuscated PowerShell confirms malice; cross-reference the device against Secure Registry to see which package version was installed. 2) Contain: isolate the host/CI runner, block the fetched URL, snapshot node_modules before it self-deletes. 3) Hunt: pivot on the resolved second-stage URL and on the C2 IOCs (23.254.164.92/.123), and enumerate every host that installed a Mastra-ecosystem package.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "npm.exe", "npm.cmd")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe", "cscript.exe", "wscript.exe", "curl.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe", "bash.exe", "wget.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "postinstall" or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://", "https://")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe", "npm.exe", "npm.cmd")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe", "cscript.exe", "wscript.exe", "curl.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "node_modules" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "postinstall" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://", "https://")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious easy-day-js typosquat package written into node_modules AIDelivery High
Detects the presence of the easy-day-js typosquat (of dayjs) being dropped into a node_modules directory on developer machines or CI runners — the initial-access artifact of the June 2026 Mastra npm supply-chain compromise. Any host with this path pulled the compromised dependency. Rationale: Uses the exact malicious package name (easy-day-js) named in the article as the typosquat added across 140+ Mastra packages — a filesystem path containing that string is an unambiguous indicator of the compromised dependency.
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security team intentionally staging the sample for analysis in a lab node_modules
  • A benign future package legitimately named similarly (low likelihood — name is the malicious artifact)
  • SCA/dependency-scanning tooling caching the package name in a report file on disk
  • Git repo containing a historical lockfile reference cloned to disk
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the exact version installed and whether the postinstall dropper ran (check for child processes of node/npm and the C2 IOCs); use Secure Registry to enumerate every machine/pipeline that pulled it. 2) Contain: isolate affected hosts, purge node_modules, remove easy-day-js from lockfiles, rotate any secrets exposed on those machines/runners. 3) Hunt: expand to all Mastra-ecosystem packages and to the sibling GitHub Actions compromises (codfish/semantic-release-action, simonecorsi/mawesome) in CI logs.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "easy-day-js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath has "easy-day-js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Package-manager dropper self-deletion inside node_modules (evidence erasure) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the anti-forensic self-deletion described in the Mastra compromise: after fetching the second stage, the postinstall dropper deletes itself to erase evidence. Flags node/npm deleting script files it just wrote under node_modules. Rationale: Grounds on the article's explicit anti-forensic claim that the dropper 'deleted itself to erase the evidence' — expressed as node/npm deleting script files under node_modules, a rare and suspicious combination distinct from normal install churn.
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • npm ci / clean-install wiping and rebuilding node_modules
  • Package upgrade removing an old dependency version's files
  • Yarn/pnpm cache pruning invoked via node
  • Build tooling that deletes generated .js artifacts under node_modules during a rebuild
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("ci","clean-install","rimraf","prune")
Response runbook
1) Triage: correlate the deletion with a preceding FileWritten of the same file and any node→shell/download spawn within seconds; check the device in Secure Registry for a recently pulled package. 2) Contain: isolate the host, preserve the disk/memory image before further churn, block the C2 IOCs. 3) Hunt: recover the deleted file from backups/VSS for analysis, and sweep the fleet for the same delete pattern plus easy-day-js and the C2 destinations.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "FileDeleted"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "npm.exe")
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".cjs" or FileName endswith ".sh"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileDeleted"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe", "npm.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".js" or TargetFileName endswith ".cjs" or TargetFileName endswith ".sh"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Known-malicious Mastra supply-chain payload file hashes on disk or in execution AIInstallation Medium
Alerts on the specific SHA256/SHA1 payload hashes tied to the easy-day-js dropper and its second stage from the Mastra npm compromise. Matches whether the artifact is written to disk or executed, giving a direct confirmation pivot for scoped hosts. Rationale: Uses the five SHA256 and one SHA1 hash IOCs supplied with the article — direct file-hash matches on the dropper/second-stage payloads are the highest-fidelity confirmation available for scoped hosts.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst holding a sample copy on an EDR-monitored analysis host
  • Backup/quarantine system retaining a copy of the flagged file
  • Threat-intel feed distributing the sample to a detonation VM
  • Hash collision (cryptographically implausible — effectively none)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the file path and initiating process; a match under node_modules or executed by node/npm confirms the supply-chain vector — enumerate the device in Secure Registry. 2) Contain: isolate the host/runner, quarantine the file, block the C2 IOCs, and rotate exposed credentials/tokens. 3) Hunt: pivot on the C2 IPs/domains and on easy-day-js across the fleet, and validate whether any second-stage persistence or lateral movement followed.
union DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 in ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf")
    or SHA1 == "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA256 in ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf")
    or TargetFileSHA1 == "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5"

title: Mastra npm compromise payload file hashes

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.254.164.92", "23.254.164.123") or RemoteUrl has_any ("teams.onweblive.org", "maskasd.com")

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5") or SHA1 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5") or MD5 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5") or SHA1 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5") or MD5 in~ ("b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b122a9873bedf145ae2a7fd024b5f309007dbb025149f4dc4ac3f7e4f32a36a4", "ae70dd4f6bc0d1c8c2848e4e6b51934626c4818dcb5af99d080ddbd7dc337185", "4a8860240e4231c3a74c81949be655a28e096a7d72f38fbe84e5b37636b98417", "b73de25c053c3225a077738a1fcbd9ca6966d7b3cd6f5494a30f0aa0eae55c7e", "221c45a790dec2a296af57969e1165a16f8f49733aeab64c0bbd768d9943badf", "6b9501e1889cc45c91726729610cf69c2442b8c5"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Multiple @immobiliarelabs Backstage Plugins Compromised on npm

StepSecurity
2026-07-01 12 use cases 3 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Compromised versions run a malicious payload at npm install time through a binding.gyp node-gyp hook, harvesting credentials from sources like GitHub Actions secrets, cloud provider keys, and package registry tokens, while trying to persist in AI coding assistant configs. Static analysis of version 2.1.2 against the clean 2.1.1 release revealed a new 5 MB index.js and an added binding.gyp, both absent from earlier releases.

Phantom Gyp binding.gyp install-time payload execution (Miasma npm worm) AIInstallation High
Hunts the GYP command-expansion shell invocation that the Miasma/Phantom Gyp worm plants in binding.gyp to run the 5 MB index.js during node-gyp configure, bypassing scripts.postinstall monitoring. The exact source line is '<!(node index.js > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo stub.c)', so a process command line carrying both 'node index.js' and 'echo stub.c' is the worm firing. Rationale: Anchored on the verbatim binding.gyp source string '<!(node index.js > /dev/null 2>&1 && echo stub.c)' from the article; the 'node index.js' + 'echo stub.c' pairing is unique to the Phantom Gyp configure-step trick and not a legitimate gyp pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/binding-gyp-npm-supply-chain-attack-spreads-like-worm • https://snyk.io/blog/node-gyp-supply-chain-compromise-self-propagating-npm-worm-binding-gyp/ • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate native addon packages whose binding.gyp uses node-based command expansion (rare; almost never invokes a bare index.js with echo stub.c)
  • Security researcher detonating the sample in a sandbox
  • CI job intentionally re-running the malicious tarball for analysis
  • A developer's own gyp build script that happens to echo a stub source file
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ProcessCommandLine and the parent chain (npm/node-gyp/sh) and identify which @immobiliarelabs (or other) package was being installed; confirm a 5 MB index.js + binding.gyp exist in that package dir. 2) Contain: isolate the host/runner, revoke any tokens that were live in that session (GitHub, npm, cloud), and rotate CI secrets exposed to the job. 3) Hunt: search the same host for a Bun binary in temp, IMDS (169.254.169.254) hits, and writes to AI-assistant configs (.claude/settings.json etc.); pivot org-wide on the affected package@version.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("node index.js", "echo stub.c")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("node index.js", "echo stub.c")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun runtime executing a temp payload spawned by node (Miasma Node.js-monitoring evasion) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the deliberate runtime switch where the Miasma loader downloads Bun (bun-v1.3.13) and runs the decrypted credential-harvester from a randomly named temp file under Bun instead of Node, to evade --require-hook security tooling. A bun process whose parent is node/npm/node-gyp/sh and that executes a file from /tmp or /var/folders is the second stage. Rationale: Uses the article's explicit detail that the loader downloads Bun (bun-v1.3.13) and executes the decrypted main payload from a randomly named temp file under Bun specifically to dodge Node's --require interception; node-parent + bun-child + temp path is the distinguishing shape. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/miasma-malware-uses-binding-gyp-and-bun/ • https://www.wiz.io/blog/miasma-supply-chain-attack-targeting-redhat-npm-packages • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/miasma-malware-targets-npm-packages-and.html
ATT&CKT1027 T1059.007 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developers who legitimately use Bun as their runtime/test-runner invoked from npm scripts
  • Bun-based build tooling executing cached transpiled output from a temp dir
  • Monorepo task runners (turbo/nx) shelling out to bun for a subpackage
  • CI images that prewarm Bun and run scratch scripts from /tmp
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the temp file path bun executed and hash it; check whether the project legitimately depends on Bun (package.json/engines) — a Bun execution with no Bun dependency declared is high-signal. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the bun process tree, and quarantine the temp payload before it self-deletes. 3) Hunt: correlate to a binding.gyp install in the prior 5 minutes, then look for IMDS/metadata access and AI-assistant config writes from the same session.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "bun" or FileName startswith "bun-"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","sh","bash","dash","npm","node-gyp","yarn","pnpm")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/","/var/folders/","/var/tmp/") or FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/","/var/folders/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "bun"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","sh","bash","dash","npm","node-gyp","yarn","pnpm")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/tmp/","/var/folders/","/var/tmp/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun Runtime Executing Temp Payload Spawned by Node (Miasma Evasion)

Miasma infectHost persistence in AI coding assistant configs AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the infectHost routine that backdoors AI coding-assistant configuration files for re-execution: .claude/settings.json (SessionStart hook), .vscode/tasks.json (folderOpen), .cursor/rules/, .aider.conf.yml, and .github/copilot-instructions.md. Filters to writes performed by node/bun/npm so legit editor saves are excluded. Rationale: Directly maps the article's infectHost target list (Claude Code SessionStart hook in .claude/settings.json, VS Code folderOpen in .vscode/tasks.json, .cursor/rules, .aider.conf.yml, .github/copilot-instructions.md); requiring a node/bun writer separates the malware from legitimate IDE saves. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/immobiliarelabs-npm-packages-compromised • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/
ATT&CKT1546 T1554
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer's VS Code / Cursor extension (which runs under node) legitimately writing tasks.json or rules on project open
  • Aider itself updating .aider.conf.yml during normal use
  • Dotfile-management tooling (chezmoi/yadm) restoring AI-assistant configs
  • An MCP/agent framework legitimately writing a SessionStart hook into .claude/settings.json
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code","cursor","aider") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code","cursor"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: open the written config and inspect the hook/command body — Miasma injects a shell/JS command into the SessionStart, folderOpen, or rules entry; benign saves contain no execution directive. 2) Contain: revert the config from version control, remove the injected hook, and isolate the host if a command was present. 3) Hunt: enumerate every repo/home dir on the host for the same five config files, and check whether the SessionStart hook already fired (child processes of the AI assistant).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/.claude/settings.json", "/.vscode/tasks.json", "/.cursor/rules", "/.aider.conf.yml", "copilot-instructions.md") or FileName in~ ("settings.json","tasks.json",".aider.conf.yml","copilot-instructions.md")
| where FolderPath has_any (".claude",".vscode",".cursor",".aider.conf.yml","copilot-instructions.md")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","npm","node-gyp")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (".claude/settings.json", ".vscode/tasks.json", ".cursor/rules", ".aider.conf.yml", "copilot-instructions.md")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","sh","bash","dash","npm","node-gyp")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
